thread:
Maya R: FYI Emberwood asked for a short canary window next week — small pilot hitting eu-west endpoints from a new edge cluster. They need a temporary egress exception + a modest RPS bump.
Samir K: Got context? what's the target RPS and duration?
Maya R: Customer says ~120 rps burst, sustained ~20 rps. Duration 10 days starting 2026-04-12. They want IPs added so traffic routes through our new peering.
Maya R: Ticket: https://redwood.support/INC-81321 (customer portal note, has their contract/renewal flag). Renewal is due in 6 weeks — product wants to avoid any perf blips.
emberwood-support-bot: Emberwood (acct: emberwood-prod) submitted onboarding form: region=eu-west, peering=false -> requesting peering + egress allowlist, canary_start=2026-04-12, canary_end=2026-04-22.
Ops Oncall: tagging @Eng Platform for kernel/throughput review. Any infra concerns for a short-lived RPS lift? :eyes:
Eng Platform: Short answer: OK if we pin to dedicated pool and enable prefix caching. Need to confirm that their IPs are safe to add to the allowlist and we have capacity headroom.
Samir K: I asked for their CIDR block and cert proof. They just replied with two /28s and a signed letter from their network team. Pasting config snippet they sent: ```json
{
  "customer": "emberwood",
  "egress_ips": ["203.0.113.32/28", "203.0.113.64/28"],
  "target_rps": 120,
  "duration_days": 10,
  "canary_policy": "10% traffic to new cluster, escalate to 50% after 48h if no errors"
}
```
Maya R: They explicitly requested that we not route through our shared public peering for the canary — they want private peering -> can we do a temporary allowlist and pin to a dedicated pool in eu-west?
Eng Platform: We can provision a dedicated mini-pool and pin traffic. Two requests: 1) add those CIDRs to egress allowlist, 2) create a rollout policy (canary -> ramp) in Console. I can create the pool but need SRE signoff for capacity commit.
Ops Oncall: From SRE perspective: capacity looks ok for 120 rps if prefix caching is enabled. Need to set safe limits: max concurrency per instance and a fallback to hosted fallback model (lower-cost variant) if latency > 400ms for >2min.
Maya R: Noted — I'll put those fallback guardrails in the rollout. Also customer flagged they might run integration tests the day prior — could we pre-warm KV cache?
Samir K: We can pre-warm by replaying a short prompt set (50 seqs) against the canary model with their test tokens. Ops: any security blockers for them providing test tokens?
Ops Oncall: Use scoped test tokens with expiry. Security reviewed similar flows, okay. Ensure logs are scoped to Emberwood for audit.
Maya R: I'll schedule a 30-min runbook call with the customer + Eng Platform on 2026-04-11 09:00 UTC. Samir, can you handle the CIDR verification and uplift the portal ticket?
Samir K: On it. I'll attach the signed network letter and add the requested config to INC-81321. I'll also ping legal for the temporary peering addendum — should be a quick approve.
emberwood-support-bot: Action items added to ticket INC-81321: add egress CIDRs, provision eu-west mini-pool, create canary rollout with fallback, generate scoped test tokens, pre-warm cache.
Maya R: Thanks everyone. If we get updates from Legal/Network, drop them in this thread. :thumbsup:
Eng Platform: I'll stand up the pool and push the canary policy draft by EOD. Leaving a note: ensure logs include token-level masking.
Ops Oncall: After Eng Platform posts draft, I'll run a quick dry-run and validate latencies. If green, we approve the short RPS bump.
Samir K: Approved to proceed from CS side. Renewal risk: keep rollout tight and share a perf snapshot with the customer after 72 hours.
Maya R: Perfect — closing coordination loop here. I'll follow up with calendar invites and attach runbook.
